No.16

Awareness of Our True Nature Beyond Modern Value Traps

When achievement brings no peace, rethinking competition, worth and our own nature.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva:

Society today overemphasizes competition, success and material measures. As a result, many people who achieve a great deal still feel empty, meaningless and depressed inside. Please give a teaching.

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"The rich have many worries, the poor have many wants; those who chase shadows forget their own true form. The world contends for fame and profit like climbing a tall tower to chase the stars — they never see the sky; those who seek outside grow farther from their heart each day. I see that beings are lost in the name of value, and do not know the substance of value. Value lies not in the judgment of others, but in the peace of the heart. If the heart has nothing to rest on, even if the whole world comes into one's hands, it is still emptiness. Therefore it is said: those whose hearts are at peace are joyful even in poverty and low station; those who have lost their hearts are withered even if they hold all under heaven.

If you wish to leave this emptiness, turn back and look at your own nature, and do not chase the tides of the world.

Replace competition with action, victory with kindness, fame with awareness; then value becomes clear of itself, and the emptiness turns into light."

🔶Plain Rendering

People today are exhausted, because society keeps promoting competition, success and material conditions — as if life only has value if you beat others, earn more and climb higher. Yet many people, even after getting these things, still feel hollow, lost, even depressed inside.

This is how the Bodhisattva taught: The rich have many worries; the poor have many cravings; those who chase a shadow with all their strength forget what they really are.

People compete for fame and profit like someone who keeps climbing a tower to pick the stars, only to find the sky farther and farther away;

those who always reach outward grow more distant from their own hearts day by day. I see that beings are often lost in the word "value", without knowing what value really is. Value has never lain in other people's opinions, but in whether your heart is at peace. If the heart has nothing to return to, even owning the whole world still feels empty. So it is said: those whose hearts are settled can live happily even in ordinary circumstances; those who have lost their hearts are withered in spirit even if they own the world.

If you want to leave this emptiness behind, turn back and look at your own true nature, and do not blindly follow society's trends.

Replace "competition" with "action", "winning and losing" with "kindness", "empty fame" with "awakening". Then you will naturally understand what true value is, and the emptiness inside will become a light that shines on you.
